item.title: New York building collapse kills 8, including 2 children
item.description:
Six adults and two children were killed Wednesday afternoon when a three-story building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed into a construction site next door. Eighteen other people were injured in the collapse or responding to it. One of them remains in critical condition, Mayor Zohran Mamdani reported at a press conference Thursday afternoon. Many of the people impacted by the collapse are immigrants, the mayor said, including from Trinidad, Colombia and Mexico. One victim was a 26-year-old father from Ecuador, Today reported . José Luis Caguana Cosquillo leaves behind his pregnant wife and their first child. Two of the people killed were construction workers working on the excavation next door at the time of the collapse, City officials said. item.title: Gaza surgeon films aftermath of Israeli strike
item.description:
Hospital director says 28 wounded in attack on one of few remaining medical facilities in the strip An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director. The Israeli military carried out the attack on the hospital, in Khan Younis, early on Thursday saying in a statement it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters there, without providing evidence. item.title: Jessica Pegula wins thrilling contest at WTA Finals, Coco Gauff eliminated
item.description:
American saves match point in 7-6, 4-6, 7-5 victory Pegula advances as compatriot Gauff is eliminated Hot-mic controversy adds spice to Andreeva semi Jessica Pegula saved a match point en route to a gritty 7-6 (7-2), 4-6, 7-5 win over Linda Noskova on Thursday to advance from her round-robin group at the WTA Finals and send fellow American Coco Gauff packing from the season-ending championships. Pegula hit a career-high 16 aces while Wimbledon champion Noskova committed a career-high 15 double faults in a see-saw battle that lasted two hours and 45 minutes at the tournament, which was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells because of the US-Israeli war on Iran. item.title: US disrupts North Korea's $400 million crypto scam, FBI says
item.description:
The US has seized servers linked to a North Korean scam that used fake video meetings and deepfakes to steal more than $400 million in crypto, and has moved to seize $1.2 billion that was taken from Binance.
